title: School open days and public relations — attracting your next intake
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on running an effective open day and building the kind of public reputation that attracts strong applicants for the next intake.
body:
September through November is peak decision-making season for Grade 9 parents choosing a senior school. How a school presents itself during this window — through an open day, word of mouth, and general public reputation — significantly shapes the following year's admission quality and numbers. This is worth deliberate attention, not something left to happen informally.

What actually influences parent decisions

Kenyan parents choosing a senior school weigh a combination of factors: academic performance reputation, fee affordability, facilities, discipline and safety reputation, and increasingly, how organised and professional the school appears in its communication and administration. A school that presents disorganised admissions processes or is difficult to get information from creates doubt regardless of its actual academic quality.

Designing an effective open day

Let current students speak

Prospective parents and students trust the perspective of current students more than any staff presentation. Well-briefed student ambassadors who can speak genuinely about their experience — academics, facilities, pastoral care — are one of the most persuasive elements of a well-run open day.

Show, don't just tell

An open day built around a static presentation with slides is far less effective than one that lets visitors genuinely see the school in action — a live classroom demonstration, laboratory facilities in use, sports facilities, dormitories for boarding schools. Tangible, visible evidence builds more confidence than descriptions alone.

Practical tip: Have clear, printed (or digital) information available for parents to take away — fee structure, admission requirements, key dates, and contact information. Parents who leave an open day without concrete next steps often lose momentum in their decision process.

Beyond the open day — ongoing reputation management

An open day is one moment in a much longer reputation-building process. Parents in a community talk to each other continuously about schools — their experiences with admissions responsiveness, fee communication clarity, and how the school handles concerns. Every interaction a parent has with your school's administration contributes to this ongoing reputation, whether or not it is an official "PR" moment.

Making your school easy to learn about

A school with an active, accurate website and clear WhatsApp or phone contact for admission enquiries is far easier for a prospective parent to engage with than one that requires an in-person visit just to get basic information. In an increasingly digital decision-making environment, an accessible online presence is now a genuine competitive factor in admissions.

Leveraging genuine results and achievements

Academic results, notable student achievements, and alumni success stories are the most credible marketing material a school has — provided they are communicated honestly and specifically, not through vague claims. Sharing these achievements through your website, social media, and community channels throughout the year, not only at admission season, builds sustained reputation rather than a one-time push.
